dependencies: Euclidean Cauchy–Schwarz; monotonicity definition; differentiable first-order convexity and concavity inequalities. Required objects are defined in this record.
proofs.full_local_argument: Fix feasible x. Choosing z=x gives gM(x)>=0 and gS(x)>=0. Monotonicity gives <F(x)-F(z),x-z>>=0 for every z in X, hence <F(z),x-z><=<F(x),x-z>. Taking suprema yields gM(x)<=gS(x). Fix any n in N_X(x). Its outward convention gives <n,z-x><=0, thus <n,x-z>>=0. For every z in X, <F(x),x-z><=<F(x)+n,x-z><=||F(x)+n|| ||x-z||<=D||F(x)+n||. Taking the supremum over z gives gS(x)<=D||F(x)+n|| for every genuine n. The cone is nonempty because it contains 0. Taking its infimum gives gS(x)<=D r_tan(x), without needing to select a minimizing normal. Compactness and continuity make the gaps finite. For the saddle claim fix feasible (u,v) and arbitrary (u',v') in U times V. Differentiable concavity gives phi(u,v')-phi(u,v)<=<grad_v phi(u,v),v'-v>. Differentiable convexity gives phi(u,v)-phi(u',v)<=<grad_u phi(u,v),u-u'>. Adding gives phi(u,v')-phi(u',v)<=<F_phi(u,v),(u,v)-(u',v')>. Taking the supremum over the independent competitors gives Gap_phi<=gS; choosing u'=u,v'=v gives Gap_phi>=0. The outward-normal diameter argument already gives gS<=D r_tan without needing monotonicity. To verify that the full VI gap chain applies as well, write x=(u,v), y=(u',v') and B=phi(u,v')-phi(u',v). The preceding inequalities give <F_phi(x),x-y>>=B. At y, convexity gives <grad_u phi(y),u-u'><=phi(u,v')-phi(u',v'), and concavity gives <-grad_v phi(y),v-v'><=phi(u',v')-phi(u',v). Adding gives <F_phi(y),x-y><=B. Subtracting proves <F_phi(x)-F_phi(y),x-y>>=0, so F_phi is monotone. These arguments hold on the stated boundaries and lower-dimensional product domains. Finally, a feasible genuine normal certificate has r_tan(x)<=||F(x)+n||<=epsilon and therefore all applicable gaps are <=D epsilon. Taking epsilon=delta_g/D proves the stated upper accuracy transfer. None of these upper inequalities implies a lower bound for the weaker gap criterion from a lower bound for tangent residual.

assumptions: x is feasible, and the normal is the genuine outward normal defined against every z in X; approximate or inward normals do not satisfy this statement's certificate hypothesis.
X is nonempty compact convex, with diameter bound in the same Euclidean norm; F is continuous and monotone. Higher-order smoothness and an oracle model are unnecessary.
For the saddle claim, X is the compact convex product U times V and phi has the differentiable convex-concave structure just specified.
statement.conclusion: 0<=gM(x)<=gS(x)<=D r_tan(x). For the saddle specialization, 0<=Gap_phi(u,v)<=gS(u,v)<=D r_tan(u,v). A feasible evaluated certificate n in N_X(x), ||F(x)+n||<=epsilon bounds all applicable gaps by D epsilon. To obtain saddle gap accuracy delta_g, a tangent upper guarantee may take epsilon=delta_g/D. No converse or generic tangent-to-gap lower-bound transfer is asserted.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let X be a nonempty compact convex subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean R^d, diam(X)<=D, D>0, and F:X->R^d continuous and monotone. For feasible x define N_X(x)={n:<n,z-x><=0 for every z in X}, r_tan(x)=inf_{n in N_X(x)}||F(x)+n||, gS(x)=sup_{z in X}<F(x),x-z>, and gM(x)=sup_{z in X}<F(z),x-z>. For the saddle specialization let X=U times V, with nonempty compact convex U,V and product Euclidean diameter <=D. Let phi be continuously differentiable on a neighborhood, convex in u and concave in v. Set F_phi(u,v)=(grad_u phi(u,v),-grad_v phi(u,v)), and Gap_phi(u,v)=sup_{v' in V}phi(u,v')-inf_{u' in U}phi(u',v)=sup_{u',v'}[phi(u,v')-phi(u',v)].
statement.parameter_domains: Finite d>=1, D>0; no p or oracle assumption. Tangent accuracy epsilon>=0 implies gap upper accuracy D epsilon.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such X,F,D and every feasible x, the inequalities hold pointwise and deterministically. For every such phi and feasible (u,v), the saddle inequality holds. Every genuine n in N_X(x) gives the certificate upper bound before taking its infimum.
